subject: Post-call: Avery Labs — Cost/pricing & latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Kim <nora.kim@averylabs.com>, Avery Labs <avery@averylabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Avery Labs — Cost/pricing & latency tradeoffs

Thanks for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary (from call)
- Primary use case: customer-facing chat assistant in the Avery mobile app (real-time chat + summarization).
- Estimated monthly token volume: TBD (Nora, you mentioned pilot then scale). We discussed ranges 50M–200M/mo.
- Latency SLO: p95 target ~300ms for user-facing chat; can tolerate up to 800ms for background batch tasks.
- Budget guidance: you asked for ballpark unit economics (target $/1M tokens) to share with finance.

Open asks / next steps
1) Nora — can you confirm a tighter monthly token estimate (pilot vs. steady-state)? especially peak qps during morning commute window.
2) Can you share whether streaming responses are required for UX (token-at-a-time streaming) vs. streaming optional?
3) I'll loop Dev and Jonas for technical sizing (dedicated vs hosted). We'll put together a short unit-econ model and pricing options (Hosted Pro / Dedicated reserved pool) for your budget target.

What we'll deliver by EOD Thurs (6/4):
- Short pricing sheet with estimated $/1M token tiers and expected latency trade-offs.
- Mutual action plan draft with milestones + procurement contacts.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_levels.xlsx (pricing tiers), mutual_action_plan.docx (draft MAP)

Thanks — talk soon,

--
Marissa Cole

From: Nora Kim <nora.kim@averylabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Avery Labs — Cost/pricing & latency tradeoffs

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few data points to help you size: 

- Pilot (Q3): ~50M tokens/month anticipated (chat usage limited to beta users).
- Steady-state (Q4): likely 120–160M tokens/month based on product roadmap and retention expectations.
- Peak: during push notifications / commute window we expect spikes to ~60–70 requests/sec (short messages, avg 120–150 tokens/request).
- Budget: leadership wants to stay in the $6k–$12k/month range for inference costs initially. Our procurement team suggested a target of ~$700/1M tokens as a benchmark — if you can get us close to that at our steady-state volumes we'd be in good shape.
- Latency: user-facing chat needs to feel live — p95 <= 300–350ms preferred. For nightly summarization/batch jobs we can tolerate up to 1s. Streaming is preferred for UX but not a hard blocker if overall latency is similar.

Also looping in our eng lead (cc'd) to keep technical questions going. We can take a vendor pricing breakdown and a draft MAP.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Avery Labs — pricing/latency notes (internal)

Internal — forwarding Nora's note above. High level takeaways and proposed approach: 

Takeaways:
- Steady-state 120–160M tokens/mo, pilot ~50M. Peak ~60–70 rps; avg 130 tokens/req.
- Target ~$700/1M tokens (Avery asks). p95 ~300–350ms target. Streaming preferred.

Proposed approach:
1) Offer two pricing pathways:
   - Hosted Pro (metered): lower upfront commitment, higher unit cost but includes streaming + autoscaling. Good for pilot and early scale.
   - Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): reserved GPU pool, predictable unit economics; can hit better $/1M token at steady-state but requires commit.
2) Performance config recommendations:
   - For user-facing chat: streaming enabled + small batch sizes (batch <= 8, max latency SLO enforced) to keep p95 under 350ms.
   - For background summarization: use batching (batch sizes 32–64) with lower-priority routing to reduce unit cost.
3) Quick unit-econ ballpark (rough):
   - Hosted Pro: ~ $1,100 / 1M tokens (with streaming and autoscaling) — pilot friendly.
   - Dedicated (reserved): with steady 120M+/mo, we can target ~$650–750 / 1M tokens depending on commit and quantization.

Action items:
- Dev: can you validate batch-size/latency trade-offs (esp. p95 at 130 tokens/req, 60 rps) and give recommended instance sizes?
- Jonas: I'll need you on the pricing note and MAP edits.

I'll draft the two-path pricing sheet and share by Thurs.

--
Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Avery Labs — pricing/latency notes (internal)

Quick tech note — validating Marissa's defaults. Summary: 
- With our current serving runtime, p95 ~300ms at 60 rps and avg 130 tokens/req is reachable with streaming + batching disabled for the critical path (continuous prefix cache + tiny batching window).
- Batch config: for lowest p95 keep batching window <= 10ms and target batch sizes of 4–8 for chat. For background jobs: batch window 50–200ms and batch sizes 32–64.
- Quantization: int8/awq options can reduce cost ~20–35% depending on quality tolerance; recommend running evals on sample prompts.
- SLO-driven pricing note: we can offer a dedicated reserved tier with pricing bands based on p95 windows (eg. p95 <= 300ms premium, p95 <= 500ms mid, p95 <= 800ms discount). See attached note.

Attachment: slo_pricing_notes.pdf

Dev
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Kim <nora.kim@averylabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Avery Labs — Cost/pricing & latency tradeoffs

Nora — thanks for the quick data, really helpful. Attached is a short two-path pricing summary (hosted vs dedicated) and a draft MAP. High level: 

- Pilot (50M/mo) recommendation: Hosted Pro to avoid commit and get streaming UX. Ballpark unit cost: $1,050 / 1M tokens (with streaming + autoscaling). Estimated pilot monthly spend ~ $52.5k (note: we will refine once we instrument real traffic; this is a conservative estimate inclusive of peak).
- Steady-state (120–160M/mo) recommendation: Redwood Dedicated. With a 12-mo commit and int8 quantization on less-sensitive models we can target $650–750 / 1M tokens (closer to your $700 target depending on final commit and model choice).
- Latency options: we can tier pricing by SLO. Hitting p95 <= 300ms will carry a premium vs p95 <= 500ms; Dev's attachment outlines exact bands.

Next steps: 
1) If this looks directionally right, can we schedule a 30-min technical sizing with your eng team next week? (https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/demo-30)
2) I'll prepare a one-page procurement packet for your finance team with expected monthly ranges and minimal contract language.
3) Jonas will follow up on MAP and deal worksheet.

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers once we have sample traces and token histograms.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
